If your last safe-output call already performed the final requested action and no further work or tool calls remain, it satisfies this requirement. 2026-11-18T10:54:12.8316532Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8318976Z Safe-output calls are write-once declarations for real downstream side effects. Do NOT use them for probing, auth tests, retries with placeholder content, or "let me see if this works" experiments. 2026-11-18T10:54:12.8321367Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8323464Z **Tool retry limit:** if a safe-output tool (for example `push_to_pull_request_branch` or `close_pull_request`) fails, try at most 2 materially different recovery approaches. If the tool still fails, call `report_incomplete` with the error and the approaches attempted, then continue with other work. Do NOT debug underlying infrastructure after repeated failures.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8325714Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8328018Z **Trust successful tool responses.** Safeoutputs records write transactions that are applied after the agent finishes. A successful safe-output tool call means the transaction was accepted for downstream application. Do NOT independently verify the effect via `gh`, `gh api`, or other GitHub read paths from the current sandbox, because those paths will not reflect future safe-output writes.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8330717Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8335461Z **Do not inspect infrastructure internals.** When a tool or command fails, do not inspect Docker sockets (`/var/run/docker.sock`), mount tables (`/proc/self/mounts`), container networking (`/proc/net`), `/host` paths, git object storage internals, or container-runtime environment internals. These are outside your control; use `report_incomplete` after the retry limit.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8337842Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8344204Z temporary_id: optional cross-reference field only for tools whose input schema declares it, including create_issue, create_discussion, and create_pull_request. Do not add it to other tools. Canonical form: '#aw_' followed by 3–12 alphanumeric or underscore characters — e.g., '#aw_abc1', '#aw_pr_fix'. Pattern: /^#?aw_[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,12}$/i (the '#' prefix is optional; bare 'aw_abc1' is accepted and normalised to '#aw_abc1' automatically). Use this form in target fields only where their schema explicitly supports temporary IDs (item_number, issue_number, parent, etc.). In body/markdown text, '#aw_abc1' references are replaced with the real issue/PR/discussion number after creation. Omit entirely when not needed.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8348987Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8356751Z **Payloads**: safeoutputs tools do NOT support `@filename` expansion. For CLI calls, prefer a complete JSON object inline as one single-quoted shell argument. Inside JSON strings, encode newlines as `\n`, double quotes as `\"`, backslashes as `\\`, and apostrophes as `\u0027`; Unicode can remain literal. Stdin is also supported: `safeoutputs <tool_name> .` reads a complete JSON object from stdin — the entire stdin content must itself be valid JSON; never pipe a raw file or raw Markdown into this bare form. To pass one field's raw text verbatim with no JSON escaping, target that single field instead: `cat file.md | safeoutputs <tool_name> --<field> .` substitutes the field's value with the raw stdin text. Never write a bare `.` as a value inside a quoted JSON literal (e.g. `{"body": .}`) — that is not valid JSON. Do not use auxiliary shell commands or temporary files to construct payloads; the `cat file | ... --field .` form above is the one sanctioned exception, for raw-text fields only. When a native safe-output function is explicitly exposed, pass the fields directly.

2026-11-18T10:54:12.8369479Z **Creating a Pull Request**
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8369850Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8370076Z To create a pull request:
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8370712Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8371956Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8374077Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8375733Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8377419Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8381168Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8382208Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8390415Z **Important**: The `branch` parameter in the create_pull_request tool **must exactly match the name of your current local git branch** — the branch you just committed to. You can verify this with `git branch --show-current`. Never invent or guess a branch name; always use the actual branch name from `git branch --show-current`. If you are on an existing branch (e.g. you checked out a PR branch), use that branch name.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8394878Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8396695Z **Important**: `create_pull_request` is not a sandbox. Every successful call records a real PR intent that can become an externally visible pull request. Never use placeholder payloads like `"test"` / `"test"` to see what happens. If you are not ready to open the real PR, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8399080Z </safe-output-tools>

Stdin support does not grant permission for redirections. Prefer inline JSON; do not use auxiliary shell commands to construct or submit it.

2026-11-18T10:54:12.8547884Z ## Who you are working for
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8548210Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8548978Z You maintain open data for Charge Line, an iPhone app that plans electric-vehicle road trips across Australia.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8550404Z The data in this repository reaches drivers once the owner merges your pull request. A wrong number can strand
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8553550Z someone between chargers, so accuracy matters more than coverage: when in doubt, leave the data as it is and say
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8555379Z what you found in the pull request or an issue.

2026-11-18T10:54:12.8556322Z

2026-11-18T10:54:12.8559477Z   heredocs or `sed -i`).
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8560246Z - **Shell:** one command at a time, from the workflow's allowed list, for example
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8561454Z   `node scripts/validate.mjs --base-ref origin/main`, `jq`, `grep`, `ls`. Don't use `cd` (you are already at the
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8563605Z   repository root), don't chain commands with `;` or `&&`, and don't use `python3`. If a command is refused, use a
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8564999Z   simpler command or another tool, and carry on with the task. A refused command is never a reason to stop.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8566352Z - **Web:** WebSearch finds pages and WebFetch reads one. A firewall lets through Australian sites (`.com.au`,
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8567647Z   `.gov.au`, `.org.au`, `.net.au`) and a few others. If a fetch is refused, that site isn't allowed: note it and
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8569928Z   move on.

2026-11-18T10:54:12.8571761Z ## Sources
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8572006Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8572601Z - **Prefer primary sources:** the maker's or network's own Australian website, then Australian government data,
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8573627Z   then The Driven (thedriven.io).
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8575064Z - **Never read these sites**, directly or through search results. Their terms forbid automated reading, or they

2026-11-18T10:54:12.8600117Z

2026-11-18T10:54:12.8605995Z # Keep charging networks and prices current
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8606412Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8606729Z `networks.json` lists Australian fast-charging networks:
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8607215Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8607818Z - **How to recognise their sites:** `match`, lower-case text found in a site's operator or name.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8609186Z - **A typical price per kWh:** `typicalPerKWh`, with its `basis`, `source` and `checked` date.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8610723Z - **Whether an agent may read the network's own website:** `siteReading`.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8611664Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8612322Z `schema/networks.schema.json` describes every field. Networks price each site differently, often by the time of
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8613764Z day, and only their apps show a site's price. So a typical price is a guide, and drivers can set their own in the
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8615240Z app. This run has two jobs: find networks new to Australia, and keep the typical prices honest.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8615957Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8616607Z ## 1. Read your memory
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8616949Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8617602Z Your memory folder is `/tmp/gh-aw/repo-memory/prices/`. Keep one file, `operators.json`, created if missing. It's
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8619534Z a list of `{ "operator", "fastSites", "firstSeen", "lastSeen", "decision", "notes" }`. `decision` is one of:
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8620298Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8620533Z - `added`: you added it as a network;
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8621180Z - `alias`: it's another name for a listed network;
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8622094Z - `site-owner`: a business or council with its own chargers, not a network drivers join;
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8623653Z - `roaming`: its sites are run through another network's app;
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8624433Z - `pending`: not decided yet.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8625693Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8625926Z ## 2. New networks
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8626381Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8627062Z `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/sources/new-operators.json` lists operators in Charge Line's public charger file with three or
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8628827Z more fast sites (50 kW or more) that no network in `networks.json` matches. For each one not already decided in
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8629809Z your memory:
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8630065Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8631477Z 1. **Find out what it is,** from the operator's own website (when its terms allow automated reading), Open Charge
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8632524Z    Map, government pages or The Driven:
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8633309Z    - a network drivers pay through its own app or card;
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8634146Z    - another name for a listed network (for example a parent company);
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8634912Z    - a site owner;
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8635437Z    - sites run through another network's app.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8636115Z 2. **A real network:** add it to `networks.json`.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8637214Z    - `id`: camelCase.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8637725Z    - `name`: as drivers know it.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8639205Z    - `match`: lower-case strings found in the operator names in the file, never one another network already uses.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8640592Z    - `typicalPerKWh`: only from a source that states the price (`basis` `published` or `survey`). Otherwise
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8641573Z      `null`, with `basis` `none`.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8642425Z    - `siteReading`: from its terms of use and robots.txt. Use `unchecked` if you couldn't tell.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8644130Z    - `source`, `sourceUrl` and `checked` (today).
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8645176Z 3. **Another name for a listed network,** or **sites run through another network's app:** add the operator's
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8646180Z    lower-case text to that network's `match`.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8646850Z 4. **A site owner:** record it in memory only.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8647266Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8647491Z ## 3. Typical prices
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8647773Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8648165Z For each network, look for evidence that its typical price has changed:
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8651661Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8652152Z - **The network's own website:** only when its `siteReading` is `allowed`.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8654268Z - **News of a price change:** The Driven, or the network's own announcements.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8655357Z - **Recent Open Charge Map listings** that state a price (checked in the last year).
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8656000Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8656748Z Change `typicalPerKWh` only when a source supports the new figure. Then update `basis`, `source`, `sourceUrl` and
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8658191Z `checked`, and give the old and new figure in the pull request. Keep `teslaPerKWh` and `freeKWhPerDay` up to date
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8660395Z the same way.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8660675Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8661279Z **When no source you may read gives a price,** and a network's `checked` date is more than six months old, open
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8662844Z an issue asking the owner to check the price in the network's app. One issue covering every such network.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8663603Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8663803Z ## 4. Propose
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8664059Z 
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8665292Z - **Changes to `networks.json`:** follow "Editing the data" and "The pull request" in the shared rules. Title it
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8666721Z   `[prices] ` plus a short summary, such as "Add Yurika; Evie typical 0.69 → 0.72".
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8667719Z - **Things only the owner can check:** open an issue. Three at most.
2026-11-18T10:54:12.8668823Z - **Nothing found:** propose nothing. Your memory is still saved.
